prediction:
THOUGHT: This elderly woman in hospice has fever, RUQ tenderness, leukocytosis, tachycardia and acute mental-status change (likely delirium from infection). Liver tests show a cholestatic pattern (elevated bilirubin and ALP) with mild transaminase elevation. Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid but no gallstones. In a debilitated/critically ill patient without stones these findings are most consistent with acute acalculous cholecystitis; ascending cholangitis is a consideration with fever/jaundice/RUQ pain but would more typically show bile duct dilation or obstructing stone/stricture on imaging. Thus the clinical picture and ultrasound strongly favor acalculous cholecystitis as the cause of infection and delirium.

DIAGNOSIS: Acute acalculous cholecystitis.
